name: mushroomed lentils italian
instructions:
The ITALIAN member of the mushroomed-lentils family — and the rule-breaker: the mushrooms are FINELY DICED, not pureed or processed (chunky, not a goo), and the dish is LIGHTER AND BROTHIER than its siblings.

=== THE BUILD ===

- MUSHROOMS: finely diced — NOT pureed, NOT food-processed. Chunky, not a goo.
- CELERY, CARROT, AND ONION: also finely diced (soffrito).
- LENTILS: whole.
- TOMATO PASTE + DARK STOCK: the backbone — the mushroomed-lentils pattern, not the minestrone whole-tomato one (see notes).
- A TOMATO (chunked) is TOLERATED — unlike the more northern siblings, which want no tomato chunk at all.
- POTATO: diced potato is ALLOWED but not required.
- SEASONINGS: this version relies more on FENNEL (seed and/or powder) and OLD BAY.
- NOT HERE: no cream/mustard/ale, no cumin/caraway (those belong to the french and german siblings).
- NOT HERE (vs minestrone): no parmesan element, no green beans, no earthy mixed greens.
notes:
=== THE RULE-BREAKER OF THE FAMILY ===

This version half-follows the mushroomed-lentils patterns — the backbone conforms (tomato paste + stock), the texture rebels:
- MUSHROOMS DICED, NOT PUREED: the family's signature move (pureed mushrooms as the gravy engine) is deliberately absent. Here the mushrooms are finely diced and stay CHUNKY — a component, not a goo.
- LIGHTER AND BROTHIER: the big difference vs [[mushroomed-lentils-french]] — the french version relies on the pureed mushrooms + cream/mustard as a FLAVOR ENGINE; this one is a lighter, brothier dish.

=== TOMATO PASTE + STOCK — THE MUSHROOMED-LENTILS BACKBONE ===

Rethought: this recipe uses TOMATO PASTE + STOCK rather than only raw tomatoes — which is another way it pulls away from the minestrone family (minestrone doesn't like tomato paste as much). So it DOES fit the mushroomed-lentils pattern after all on the backbone (tomato paste + stock, not whole tomato). Dark stock works here even though the italian register normally resists it: MUSHROOMS AND LENTILS PAIR WELL WITH STOCK — unlike white beans, which want the tomato-only treatment.

THE TOMATO-CHUNK TOLERANCE: where this version does break from the family — it can TOLERATE A TOMATO in it (chunked), unlike the more northern versions (french/german/british), which want no tomato chunk at all.

=== SEASONINGS — FENNEL + OLD BAY ===

This version leans on seasonings where its siblings lean on balancer kits: FENNEL SEED/POWDER and OLD BAY. No cream/mustard (french kit), no ale/pickle (german kit), no cumin/caraway (german seeds).

=== VS MINESTRONE ===

Distinct from [[minestrone-soup]] despite the italian soffrito + legume shape: no parmesan cheese element, no green beans, no earthy mixed greens — and stock where minestrone stays tomato-only.

=== THE FAMILY ===

- [[mushroomed-lentils-french]]: pureed mushrooms + cream/mustard flavor engine — the rich pole; this is the light pole.
- [[mushroomed-lentils-german]]: ale + pickle + cumin/caraway.
- [[mushroomed-lentils-british]]: the wellington (A) and the pub stew (B — rosemary/thyme/lemon/potato + ale/marmite).
